{{Infobox NCAA Athlete | color = LightSteelBlue | fontcolor = Black | name = DeJuan Blair | image = Replace this image male.svg | caption = | college = [[University of Pittsburgh|Pittsburgh]] | conference = [[Big East Conference|Big East]] | sport = [[Basketball]] | jersey = 45 | position = Center | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 6.5 | weight_lb = 277 | career_start = 2007 | career_end = 2009 | nationality = USA | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1989|4|22|mf=y}} | birth_place = [[Pittsburgh]], [[Pennsylvania]] | highschool = [[Schenley High School]], Pittsburgh | awards = 2009 [[Big East Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East Player of the Year]] (with [[Hasheem Thabeet]]) 2009 [[2009 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|First team All-American]] }} '''DeJuan Blair''' (born April 22, 1989 in [[Pittsburgh]], [[Pennsylvania]]) is an [[All-American]] [[college basketball]] player. He played [[center (basketball)|center]] for the [[University of Pittsburgh]] [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|men's basketball team]]. from 2007 to 2009[http://pittsburghpanthers.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/blair_dejuan00.html] Profile on the University's athletic site and entered the [[2009 NBA Draft]] after an outstanding sophomore (second) season at Pitt. {{Citation | last = Gladysz | first = Mike | author-link = | last2 = | first2 = | author2-link = | title = As Blair Thrives, NBA dreams become a possibility | newspaper = The Pitt News | pages = 10–11 | year = 2009 | date = 2-24 | url = http://www.pittnews.com/sports/as_blair_continues_to_thrive%252C_nba_becomes_possible-1.1569324 }} ==Early years== Blair, the youngest of four children (one of whom died in infancy), grew up in Pittsburgh's [[Hill District]], literally in the shadow of the university—his childhood home is a mere {{convert|600|yard|m|sf=2}} from the Pitt campus.{{cite web |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/columns/story?columnist=oneil_dana&id=3865922 |title=Just a short walk from home, local boy Blair makes good with Panthers |first=Dana |last=O'Neil |publisher=''ESPN.com'' |date=2009-01-28 |accessdate=2009-02-26}} Although he was the smallest of his siblings at birth, he was the largest child in his class by the time he started school. Basketball was, figuratively speaking, in his blood—both of his parents played at [[Schenley High School]], which was located in the Hill District until 2007, and his uncle ran the nearby Ammons Recreation Center, where he learned to play the game. ==High school career== Blair played as a four year starter at Schenley High. While there he scored 1,563 career points and finished with an overall 103–16 team record, including a 57–0 record within the [[Pittsburgh City League]]. He was named the [[Associated Press|AP]] player of the state and made first team all state his junior and senior year. Blair led Schenley to the 2007 PIAA Class 4A state championship, the first state title for a City League team since 1978; in the final against [[Chester High School (Chester, Pennsylvania)|Chester]] (and his future Pitt teammate Nasir Robinson), he had 18 points, 23 rebounds, and 6 blocked shots. He was also named Pittsburgh City League Player of the year three times. Blair's basketball accomplishments were not limited to school. He also played in the summer leagues at Pittsburgh's Kennard Park, known for their rugged competition. Blair remembered a championship game in which his team played against a team led by current [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State]] [[quarterback]] [[Terrelle Pryor]], who was also a highly regarded basketball prospect: "They were taking bets — I got DeJuan, I got Terrelle. I had 56 that night. We won." ===Recruiting=== Blair was heavily recruited coming out of high school. Besides Pitt, other schools pursuing him included [[University of Florida|Florida]], [[Kansas State University|Kansas State]], [[Indiana University|Indiana]], [[Marquette University|Marquette]], [[University of Miami|Miami]], [[West Virginia University|West Virginia]], [[Wake Forest University|Wake Forest]] and [[University of Tennessee|Tennessee]]. His parents admitted that if they had their way, Blair would have gone to Tennessee. They liked [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Volunteers]] coach [[Bruce Pearl]], and thought it would be a good idea for their son to leave the city. Blair himself had problems making up his mind; while considering as many as 18 different [[athletic scholarship|scholarship]] offers, he was so confused that one day he threw his [[mobile phone|cell phone]] across a room, breaking it. However, neither Blair nor his parents were a match for his maternal grandmother Donna Saddler, who had played a major role in his upbringing. Pitt coach [[Jamie Dixon]] recognized Saddler's importance early in the recruiting process. On the first day he was allowed to contact Blair, he called Saddler, asking to come to her house. She told Dixon that they were having a [[family reunion]] at the house that day, and invited him to come, which he did. When Dixon was down to his last scholarship in the 2007 recruiting cycle, he called her, telling her that Blair would need to take the scholarship at that time. In the end, Saddler made the decision for him, telling him "Pitt is it." She liked Dixon and the proximity of her home to the school. Also, she was well aware that Pitt would be losing starting center [[Aaron Gray]] to graduation, which would have made Blair a likely candidate to start if he attended. He officially announced his decision to attend Pitt at the Ammons Recreation Center, where his basketball journey began, and became the first City League player to play for Pitt since Darelle Porter from 1987–1991. ==College career== ===2007–2008=== As his grandmother anticipated, Blair became the starter in his freshman year, and has remained the starter since. During his freshman year in the 2007–2008 season he played very well, earning [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American Freshman team]]. He helped the Panthers win the [[2008 Big East Men's Basketball Tournament|Big East Conference tournament]] and secure a four seed in the [[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA tournament]]. The Panthers won their first round game against Oral Roberts but lost in the second round to fifth seed [[Michigan State University|Michigan State]]. ===2008–2009=== In the 2008–2009 season, Blair has continued his dominance. He is currently third in the nation in rebounds and has been one of the most dominant centers in basketball. He has been mentioned as a possible 1st team All-American candidate and has been a large factor in Pittsburgh's season so far. In 2009 when Blair had a [[double-double]] the Panthers were 20–1, the sole loss to [[Villanova Wildcats|Villanova]] in the elite eight. When he didn't have a double-double the Panthers were 6–4. The Panthers were a number one seed for the NCAA tournament thanks in part to Blair's talent. An unnamed scout from the [[Phoenix Suns]] said if Blair develops a better mid-range shot his stock in the draft will skyrocket. Blair and [[University of Connecticut]] star [[Hasheem Thabeet]] shared co-[[Big East Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East Player of the Year]] awards for the 2008–2009 season. He was a consensus [[2009 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|First team All-American]] having been selected by [[Associated Press|AP]], [[United States Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]] and ''[[The Sporting News]]'', and the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC's]] second team. {{cite web |url=http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/awards/allamerica/index.html |title=USBWA > All-America |publisher=United States Basketball Writers Association |accessdate=2009-03-17}}{{cite web |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=526662 |title=Sporting News 2008-09 College Basketball All-Americans |publisher=Sporting News |accessdate=2009-03-17}} DeJuan also finished tied for second with [[Tyler Hansborough]] for the 2009 [[AP college basketball player of the year]] award. DeJuan received two votes, well behind the winner, [[Blake Griffin]], who received 66 votes. {{cite web |url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/news?slug=ap-applayeroftheyear&prov=ap&type=lgns |title=Oklahoma's Griffin is AP's player of the year |publisher=rivals.com |accessdate=2009-04-02}} Blair declared his intentions to enter the [[2009 NBA Draft]] on April 7th, but he has not hired an agent. {{cite web |url=http://collegebasketball.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=930947 |title=Underclassmen tracker |publisher=rivals.com |accessdate=2009-04-07}} However in a news conference the following day he announced he would be hiring an agent, forgoing any chance of returning to the school next year. {{cite web |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/draft2009/news/story?id=4052755 |title=Pitt's Blair declares for NBA draft |publisher=ESPN |access date=2009-04-08}} ===College statistics=== {| class="wikitable collapsible" width="65%" style="background:transparent" !

|} ==Impact on the city of Pittsburgh== Blair is known not only for his basketball prowess, but also for his outsized personality. His grandmother said that as a boy, he "didn't want to hurt the other kids" while playing basketball. [[ESPN]] columnist Dana O'Neil wrote about him, "He is a people collector, attracting fans and friends as he walks through his neighborhood, across campus and on the court." Blair is one of the most recognizable people in the city; his uncle Michael Smith, who taught him to play basketball, recently said, {{cquote|You ride through here with him, you get tired of beeping the horn. Everybody likes him. I can't explain how much he means to people around here. I liked the other schools and coaches he was looking at, but what did they have that he couldn't get in his own backyard? I told him he had the chance to change the face of an entire city. I truly believe that he can and he will.}} After the 2008–09 season, Dixon will launch a program in which Pitt players will mentor children from the Hill District. He saw Blair's presence as a perfect opportunity to start the program — "We've been talking about doing it for a long time. But now is the perfect time. If we can't get it going with this guy, when can we?" For his own part, Blair has said, "Someone once said to me that I'm doing for the city of Pittsburgh what [[Barack Obama|Barack [Obama]]] is doing for the United States. I didn't even know what to say. That's just crazy." If Blair does make the NBA, he will be the first NBA player to come out of the city since [[Danny Fortson]] in 1997, and the first with deep roots in the city—birth, city high school, and college—since [[Mel Bennett]] in the 1970s.
